item.title: Mean-field BSDEs with jumps under quadratic-exponential growth
item.description: arXiv:2611.13051v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the well-posedness of mean-field backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs, for short) with Poisson jumps, where the generator has quadratic growth with respect to $Z$ and exponential growth with respect to $U$, where $(Y,Z,U)$ denotes the solution of this BSDE. First, we prove the existence and the uniqueness of local solutions to mean-field backward stochastic differential equations with jumps (BSDEJs, for short) by using a fixed-point argument. Then, based on these local results, we discuss the solvability of global solutions in the following two cases: in the first one, the generator has linear growth with respect to $Y$ and the corresponding marginal distribution $\mu_1$; and in the second one, the generator has subquadratic growth with respect to the marginal distribution $\mu_2$ and linear growth with respect to the marginal distribution $\mu_3$, corresponding to $Z$ and $U$, respectively. Finally, by employing a Girsanov transformation we establish a comparison theorem for mean-field BSDEJs under quadratic-exponential growth conditions.
item.dc:creator: Weimin Jiang, Juan Li, Yan Shen

item.title: Sharp and explicit Berry--Esseen inequalities over convex sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.13106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish finite-sample Berry--Esseen bounds over all convex subsets of $\R^{d}$ for sums of independent random vectors. The upper bounds give explicit dependence on the sample size, dimension, and moments of the summands, with numerical constants. They allow arbitrary dependence among coordinates and cover every real moment order from three onward. For i.i.d. summands, we determine the optimal dependence of the worst-case error on the sample size, the dimension, and the prescribed moment bound. We obtain matching lower bounds using bounded distributions that can be chosen independently of the sample size. The results reveal a fourth-moment threshold for normal approximation over convex sets. Four is the first moment order for which uniform bounds on the corresponding coordinate moments yield a worst-case error bound linear in the dimension. Bounds on higher moments give the same worst-case rate. The proof combines convexity with the addition of independent Gaussian noise to establish a normal approximation bound for Rademacher sums on Parseval frames. Random swaps with independent copies then allow us to apply this bound conditionally to general sums of independent random vectors.
item.dc:creator: Mayya Zhilova

item.title: Bi-parameter local linearization and parameter estimation for the damped stochastic Klein--Gordon equation with spatially colored noise
item.description: arXiv:2611.13432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider the one-dimensional nonlinear damped stochastic Klein--Gordon equation driven by Gaussian noise that is white in time and fractional in space, with Hurst parameter $H\in(1/2,1)$. For a globally Lipschitz diffusion coefficient, we approximate characteristic mixed increments by those of the additive equation, multiplied by the coefficient frozen at the base point. A critical-kernel reduction and localized Riesz covariance estimates control the additional kernel terms and spatial correlations. We also establish $L^p$ error bounds for normalized quadratic variations and, under a nondegeneracy condition, construct jointly strongly consistent estimators of the Hurst parameter and a positive diffusion parameter.
item.dc:creator: Yumeng Li, Ran Wang

item.title: Entropy maximization for cube projections
item.description: arXiv:2611.13533v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, in every dimension $n\ge150$, the one-dimensional projections of the uniform distribution on a cube have the largest differential entropy in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. This establishes the conjecture of Eskenazis, Nayar, and Tkocz in these dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Zhekai Pang

item.title: Tail Asymptotics for Gaps in Unitary Ensembles and the Airy Point Process
item.description: arXiv:2611.13666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive tail asymptotics for the gap between the $k$th and $(k+1)$st largest particles, with $k$ fixed, in unitary ensembles and in the Airy point process. For the finite-$N$ ensembles, we consider the probabilities of a rescaled gap larger than $a_N$ and of a rescaled gap smaller than $b_N$, in the joint limits $N\to\infty$, $a_N\to\infty$ with $a_N=o(N^{2/3})$, and $N\to\infty$, $b_N\downarrow0$, respectively. For the Airy point process, the right and left tails are analyzed as the gap size tends to infinity and zero, respectively. More precisely, in both models, we obtain logarithmic right-tail asymptotics up to the constant term and cubic left-tail asymptotics with coefficient $k/6$. As an application, we also derive the limiting conditional laws of the leading particles given the existence of an abnormally large or small gap. In particular, for $k=1$, large-gap conditioning leads to a transition from Tracy--Widom to Gaussian fluctuations of the largest particle, similar to the BBP transition. Further, among any fixed number of leading gaps, we also determine the limiting probabilities of which gap attains a large maximum or a small minimum.
item.dc:creator: Junwen Liu

item.title: Stochastic homogenization of $p$-resistance forms on nested fractals
item.description: arXiv:2611.13724v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the stochastic homogenization of $p$-energies on infinite nested fractals. We assign i.i.d. random $p$-resistance forms $D_{0,\alpha}$ to level-$0$ cells of an infinite pre-nested fractal, and study the scaling limit of the resulting random $p$-resistance form $\mathcal{D}^{(0)}$. Under a moment condition on the reciprocal of $D_{0,\alpha}$, we prove that the sequence of rescaled and renormalized random energies is almost surely Mosco convergent to an equally weighted self-similar $p$-resistance form. As an application, when $p=2$, we prove the almost sure weak convergence of the associated rescaled continuous-time random walk. In particular, we allow arbitrarily small random conductances and impose no condition on the upper bound of random conductances.
item.dc:creator: Shiping Cao, Haiping Jiao, Hua Qiu

item.title: Multivariate Bernstein duality for tournament Wright--Fisher diffusions
item.description: arXiv:2611.13731v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a probabilistic proof of a multivariate Bernstein duality for a multivariate Wright--Fisher frequency process with selection encoded by a finite tournament. The construction includes nontransitive interactions, such as rock--paper--scissors selection. Its dual is a pure-jump process of coefficient functions in the multinomial Bernstein basis. Selection increases the Bernstein degree through a winner--loser averaging operator, whereas neutral resampling decreases it through a duplication operator. For the proof, we construct a continuous forward process independently of duality, use duality to establish uniqueness, and obtain a weak stochastic differential equation representation and invariance of the simplex faces. This provides a sampling-based treatment of the tournament specialization of multitype Bernstein duality, extending an open problem in the binary Kingman setting of Cordero, Hummel, and Schertzer (2022).
item.dc:creator: Osvaldo Angtuncio Hern\'andez

item.title: Besicovitch-like Pseudo Almost Automorphic Stochastic Processes: Theory and Applications to Semilinear SDEs
item.description: arXiv:2611.13775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces, for the first time, the concept of Besicovitch-like pseudo almost automorphic stochastic processes. As a meaningful application, we investigate a class of semilinear stochastic equations driven by Brownian motion in a separable Hilbert space. By combining the Banach fixed point theorem with refined inequality techniques, we establish sufficient conditions guaranteeing the existence, uniqueness, and global exponential stability of Besicovitch-like pseudo almost automorphic solutions in distribution for the considered equations. An example is provided to show the validity of the obtained results.
item.dc:creator: Yongkun Li, Yuwei Cao

item.title: Uniqueness of generalized conformal restriction measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.13809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide a new and unified approach (called the SLE arc test) for proving the uniqueness of generalized chordal and radial conformal restriction measures for $c\le 1$, where the $c<-2$ case is unknown before. This approach is inspired by the completely conformally invariant (CCI) measure introduced by Lawler and Werner (2000), and also by Cai's recent Green's function test for the Brownian loop catcher (2026).
item.dc:creator: Zhuoyan Xie

item.title: Transforms between multivariate Laguerre and Meixner polynomials and their applications to gateways
item.description: arXiv:2611.13932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish gateways in both directions between the Laguerre process and a discrete Markov process for every inverse temperature $2\theta \geq 1$. Here, a gateway is an intertwining relation between Markov processes with continuous and discrete state spaces. A key ingredient is a pair of generating function identities that relate two double generating functions for multivariate Meixner polynomials to a single and a double generating function for multivariate Laguerre polynomials, respectively. These identities reveal a close relationship between the two families of polynomials and yield integral transforms that underlie the gateway relations. Gateway relations provide a means of transferring properties between continuous and discrete processes. As an application, we derive the Feller-Dynkin property and the uniqueness of the invariant distribution for the Laguerre process from the corresponding properties of the discrete process.
item.dc:creator: Yosuke Kawamoto, Genki Shibukawa

item.title: Energy Dissipation Along Trajectories and Wasserstein Gradient Flow of Aggregation-Diffusion Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we established the Wasserstein gradient flow structure of nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations on bounded domains involving both nonlinear diffusion and nonlocal interaction effects. Our approach is based on stochastic analysis. More precisely, we investigated the associated stochastic differential equation (SDE) with normal reflection at the boundary from a trajectorial perspective and derived a semimartingale decomposition of the corresponding energy process. This decomposition leads to a trajectorial energy dissipation identity, which, together with the characterization of the metric derivative, allows us to establish the Wasserstein gradient flow structure of the aggregation-diffusion equation.
item.dc:creator: Honglei Chen, Xuewei Wang

item.title: Random Laguerre tessellations in hyperbolic space
item.description: arXiv:2611.14063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Laguerre tessellations in hyperbolic space as a weighted generalization of Voronoi tessellations and a hyperbolic analogue of Euclidean power diagrams. We present geometric and analytic constructions and establish conditions under which a collection of weighted points generates a well-defined tessellation. For Poisson point processes of weighted points, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions on the intensity measure ensuring that the resulting diagram is almost surely a tessellation. We then prove that hyperbolic Poisson-Laguerre tessellations are stable under intersections with totally geodesic subspaces, with an explicit transformation of the intensity measure. As applications, we identify the Poisson-Laguerre tessellations arising as sections of hyperbolic Poisson-Voronoi and ideal Poisson-Voronoi tessellations. In particular, the latter have unbounded cells, while their proper totally geodesic sections have bounded cells almost surely.
item.dc:creator: Anna Gusakova, Panagiotis Spanos

item.title: Integration by parts and DLR equations for SPDEs on the whole line
item.description: arXiv:2611.14199v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a stochastic reaction-diffusion equation on the whole real line, driven by space-time white noise, with a possibly nonlocal diffusion operator, such as a fractional Laplacian, and a coercive potential with polynomial growth. On the whole line, unlike on bounded intervals, its invariant measures cannot be described by an explicit density with respect to a Gaussian measure. We set the equation in suitable weighted spaces and show that invariant and infinitesimally invariant measures coincide, as do reversible measures and solutions to an integration-by-parts formula. We then show that the reversible measures are exactly the Gibbs measures defined through the Dobrushin-Lanford-Ruelle equations, without any moment condition, thanks to a priori estimates that also yield a Fernique-type theorem, uniform with respect to translations. In this way, we connect the Da Prato-Zabczyk approach to invariant measures of SPDEs with the DLR approach from statistical mechanics to Gibbs measures. Finally, we prove the existence of a reflection positive reversible measure and, in analogy with the one-dimensional long-range Ising model, we show that the reversible measure is unique, ergodic and translation invariant when the kernel of the nonlocal operator has a finite first moment, while it can be non-unique, for suitable double-well potentials, when the kernel has a power-law decay with infinite first moment.
item.dc:creator: Davide A. Bignamini, Francesco C. De Vecchi, Carlos Villanueva Mariz

item.title: Average and probabilistic linear widths of sequence spaces with a Gaussian measure
item.description: arXiv:2611.14216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\gamma$ be a Gaussian measure on the sequence space $\ell_2$ whose mean is zero and whose correlation operator $C_\gamma$ is a diagonal operator on $\ell_2$. Exact values of the $q$-average linear $n$-widths in $\ell_q$ for $1\le q<\infty$ are obtained. We also obtain asymptotic orders of the average linear $n$-width in $\ell_\infty$ under some condition on $C_\gamma$, and of the probabilistic linear $(n,\delta)$-widths in $\ell_q$ for $1\le q\le 2$, and for $2<q\le \infty$ under some condition on $C_\gamma$.
item.dc:creator: Yun Ling, Heping Wang

item.title: Composite local observables of sine-Gordon via stochastic analysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.14296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a rigorous framework for the description of general local composite observables in Euclidean quantum field theories. The approach is nonperturbative and combines renormalisation group ideas with techniques of stochastic analysis. Via renormalisation dictated by sufficiently precise approximate solution theory of corresponding flow equations, we construct various local observables of the sine-Gordon model on the full space up to $\beta^2<6\pi$, including highly singular ones such as vertex fields $\exp(i\alpha\phi(y))$ in the optimal Wick regime $|\operatorname{Re}(\alpha)|<4\pi/\beta$ and derivatives of arbitrarily high order, i.e. $\partial^\mu\phi(y)$ for any multiindex $\mu\in \mathbb{N}^2_0$. Applications of the approach include a direct proof of smoothness of observable-inserted correlation functions, and verification that the constructed objects satisfy a version of the prefactorization algebra axioms adapted to our setting.
item.dc:creator: Massimiliano Gubinelli, Peter Paulovics

item.title: Long-time behaviour of solutions for equations with randomness
item.description: arXiv:2611.14396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss results on the mixing properties of solutions for discrete and continuous time equations, drived by stationary bounded random forces, obtained during the last three years in a number or our joint papers. To facilitate applications of these results to specific equations with randomness, the results are edited and properly re-arranged.
item.dc:creator: Sergei Kuksin

item.title: Phase transitions in the hard-wall large deviations for the Gaussian free field
item.description: arXiv:2611.14448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the probability that the Gaussian free field on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\ge3$, stays above a level $-h_N$ throughout the lattice $N$-blow-up of a bounded Lipschitz domain, when $h_N$ is close to the entropic-repulsion height $\sqrt{4g_0\log N}$. Two mechanisms compete: a collective upward displacement of the field, whose cost is governed by capacity, and the suppression of the remaining local violations, whose cost is their expected number, both of which are of order $N^{d-2}/\log N$ exactly in the window $h_N(\beta)^2=g_0(4\log N+\log\log N+2\beta)$. We obtain a sharp asymptotic rate expressed through a variational problem combining a Dirichlet energy with an exponential potential inside this critical window. Outside this window we obtain the asymptotics at the appropriate moving speeds: capacity alone governs the cost as $\beta\to-\infty$, and the expected number of violations as $\beta\to+\infty$. As an application, we derive lower-deviation bounds for the cover level of a macroscopic body by random interlacements, which determine the order of decay at the transition.
item.dc:creator: Xinyi Li, Jialu Shi

item.title: The expected number of holes of the planar Wiener sausage
item.description: arXiv:2611.14500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: ```text Let $\beta_1^T(r)$ be the number of holes, that is, the first Betti number, of the Wiener sausage of radius $r$ of a planar Brownian motion run up to time $T$. We prove that $\mathbb{E}[\beta_1^T(r)]$ is of order $T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$ as $T\to\infty$, for each fixed $r>0$, which completes the lower bound obtained in a companion paper from a law for the inradii of the cavities of the path. We also identify which parts of the complement of the path contribute at leading order. At unit time and radius $\varepsilon$, the holes lying in the unbounded component of the complement have expected number $O(\varepsilon^{-2+\theta_0})$ for an absolute $\theta_0>0$, whereas the additional holes created when a cavity fragments under erosion have expected number of exact order $\varepsilon^{-2}(\log(1/\varepsilon))^{-2}$. In particular the one-pocket constant of the lower bound is strictly improved. The upper bound is obtained by pricing the contact configurations that pin near-critical pockets along the two independent arms of the path from a deterministic time, each arm contributing one factor $1/\log(1/\varepsilon)$. The outer estimate combines a stratified form of this first-moment bound with a packing argument near the frontier of the path, and the splitting lower bound forces a dumbbell-shaped cavity by a local construction followed by two logarithmic avoidance probabilities. The upper bound and the two structural estimates use no limit theorem for the shapes of cavities; the shape law enters only through the lower bound of the companion paper. ```
item.dc:creator: Tristan Guillaume (CY Cergy Paris University)

item.title: Lorentzian entropy, subgaussian matrix concentration, and sharp functional inequalities for all matroids
item.description: arXiv:2611.00626v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove complete entropy contraction for homogeneous Lorentzian laws and derive subgaussian matrix concentration and sharp functional inequalities for every matroid. Uniform retention of $\ell$ out of $r$ particles contracts matrix entropy by the optimal universal factor $\ell/r$, in every finite matrix dimension and positive field, including repeated labels. The matrix Laplace comparison retains matrix variance and arbitrary Hermitian offsets. It gives subgaussian bounds for arbitrary Hermitian observables with bounded exchange differences, and Chernoff and Bernstein bounds for basis sums. Every unit-edge matroid basis graph satisfies the cube's small-set and Gross inequalities, with equality classified and optimal universal complete entropy-decay rate four. Its spectrum lies in $\{0,2\}\cup[3,\infty)$, with binary direct-factor contrasts spanning the eigenspace at two. We classify extremal down-up eigenfunctions, resolving Alaniz Pintos's degree-one conjecture and the equality problem for the Feder--Mihail walk. For degree at least two, every matrix entropy extremizer extends uniquely from its two-particle marginal. Equality depends only on the normalized pair law, with noncommutativity confined to mutually exclusive labels. We classify power-entropy extremizers for $1<p<2$ and give a fourth-order criterion for affine equality. Retained-level Gibbs reconstruction has sharp dimension-independent stability. For multiaffine laws whose generating polynomial and complement are Lorentzian, we determine the exact simultaneous all-field quantum marginal and matrix H\"older regions and classify the sharp half-marginal fields. Connected sharp laws are determinantal through rank three; stable nondeterminantal examples exist in every higher rank.
item.dc:creator: Eren Ercan

item.title: A Markovian SuASR epidemic framework with stochastic external factors
item.description: arXiv:2611.12989v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Epidemic waves are often shaped by uncertain external drivers, such as environmental variability or behavioral and policy changes, that can randomly amplify or dampen transmission. Capturing this randomness requires models whose dynamics evolve under time-varying, stochastic influences. In this paper, we introduce a stochastic Susceptible-Asymptomatic-Symptomatic-Removed (SuASR) framework that embeds random external factors directly into the epidemic mechanism through an extended continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC). The proposed framework is flexible enough to represent epidemic dynamics both with reinfection and with infection-induced immunity, depending on the epidemiological setting under study. Unlike standard Markovian epidemic models, our formulation explicitly tracks two concurrent infectious sources (asymptomatic and symptomatic), yielding coupled infection pathways and substantially richer transient behavior. A key contribution is analytical tractability, where we derive computable expressions for the joint distribution of asymptomatic and symptomatic infection-event counts and develop tools tailored to extreme-outbreak risk, including the distribution of the maximum infectious burden. These results enable probabilistic quantification of epidemic severity beyond mean trajectories, providing direct estimates of the likelihood of rare but consequential surges. We validate the model through extensive sensitivity analysis and an application to the H1N1 influenza epidemic, illustrating how stochastic external influences reshape outbreak profiles, total infections from both sources, and the probability of extreme epidemic scenarios
item.dc:creator: Vasileios E. Papageorgiou, Georgios Vasiliadis

item.title: On the Concavity of R\'enyi Entropy and R\'enyi Entropy Power along Heat Flows on Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.13040v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we establish the concavity of R\'enyi entropy and R\'enyi entropy power along heat flow on Euclidean space of arbitrary dimension, for R\'enyi orders $\alpha\in[1,2]$. More generally, we prove the corresponding result along the heat flow generated by the Witten Laplacian on complete Riemannian manifolds under a suitable curvature-dimension condition. Our argument builds on novel functional inequalities that were recently developed for the study of Tsallis entropy concavity along the heat flow. We extend both these inequalities and the resulting concavity theorem from the Euclidean setting to the Riemannian manifold setting. In addition, we establish the complete monotonicity of Tsallis entropy of order $2$ along the heat flow and derive its spectral decomposition.
item.dc:creator: Hao Wu, Lei Yu

item.title: Microscopic derivation of the classical KMS condition for one-dimensional Bose gases
item.description: arXiv:2611.13124v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Kubo--Martin--Schwinger (KMS) condition provides an intrinsic characterization of thermal equilibrium, both in quantum and classical statistical mechanics. In this work, we establish stability of the KMS condition through the quantum-to-classical limit for one-dimensional defocusing Bose gases. More precisely, we consider scaled quantum KMS states in the (mean-field) semiclassical regime and prove that every associated Wigner measure satisfies the classical KMS condition corresponding to the nonlinear Schr\"odinger Hamiltonian. This result extends to an infinite-dimensional setting an earlier derivation of the classical KMS condition for finite-dimensional Bose--Hubbard systems. It also provides a complementary perspective on the derivation of nonlinear Gibbs measures from many-body quantum statistical mechanics.
item.dc:creator: Zied Ammari, Shahnaz Farhat, S\"oren Petrat, Andrew Rout

item.title: Rotating Walks, Derandomized Squares, and Permutation Conjugated Walks
item.description: arXiv:2611.13693v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using the recent strong convergence results of Bordenave and Collins (Annals of Mathematics) and Chen et al. (Annals of Mathematics), we study the average case behavior of rotating random walks of Cohen and Maor (STOC 2023) and the derandomized square construction of Rozenman and Vadhan (RANDOM 2005). Concretely, we prove a conjecture of Cohen et al. (ITCS 2025) regarding the average case behavior of derandomized squaring for random graphs and show that the existential bounds of Cohen and Maor for their rotating random walk construction hold with high-probability for random graphs. Using the results of O'Donnell and Wu (FOCS 2020), we can in polynomial time construct a family of graphs and rotations which almost saturate the bounds of Cohen and Maor, and meet the bounds conjectured by Cohen et al. for all vertex-transitive auxiliary graphs of fixed degree in the derandomized square. Finally, we study independent random permutation conjugates of deterministic regular graph adjacency matrices. We prove quantitative weak convergence to freely independent tree adjacency operators when the degrees are fixed and the girths tend to infinity. Separately, a covering argument gives deterministic spectral lower bounds for polynomials with non-negative coefficients, recovering the lower bound of Cohen et al. for rotating walks.
item.dc:creator: Vedat Levi Alev, Shravas Rao

item.title: Mean Curvature Flow with Thermal Fluctuations in Dimensions Two and Higher
item.description:
arXiv:2611.13703v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Surface tension drives interfaces towards smaller area, while thermal motion produces shape fluctuations whose strength is linked to the interfacial mobility through the fluctuation--dissipation relation. These mechanisms lead to mean-curvature flow with thermal noise, whose graph formulation is known as the Kawasaki--Ohta equation. We establish global-in-time existence of energy martingale solutions to the spatially regularized Kawasaki--Ohta equation for periodic graphs in every dimension $d\geq2$, with initial data in $H^1(\mathbb T^d)$. No restriction on the noise intensity is needed for $d=2$, while a smallness condition is required for $d\geq3$. The key new challenges arise from the thermal noise, which has a $(1+|
abla u|^2)^{1/4}$-type coefficient. This coefficient gives rise to an irregular Stratonovich-to-It\^o correction term of the form $
abla u\cdot D^2u
abla u/(1+|
abla u|^2)^{3/2}$. Our main innovation is a compactness argument tailored to the structure of the correction. By combining a factorization of this term with $H^1(\mathbb T^d)$ and area estimates, we establish strong convergence of the normalized gradients and reconstruct the weighted Hessian, which allows us to define the correction at energy regularity and identify its approximation limit.
item.dc:creator: Zhengyan Wu, Ao Zhang

item.title: Nonzero-Sum Stochastic Exit Games with Singular Belief Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.13841v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a two-player nonzero-sum stochastic exit game with asymmetric information. Each firm chooses the time to exit a duopoly and, conditional on remaining active, when to exit a monopoly. The asymmetry stems from privately observed exit values, while profit flows are driven by a general one-dimensional diffusion. Allowing for exit from monopoly induces singular dynamics of the associated belief process, so we construct it as a limit of regular approximations. The underlying dynamics are not described by a system of SDEs, which requires a new mathematical approach. We construct a symmetric Nash equilibrium in which the duopoly exit is a hitting time of the belief process while the monopoly exit is described through the underlying diffusion. Our equilibrium exhibits novel phenomena: the market may be abandoned by both firms in finite time (market collapse), and firms with heterogeneous exit values may optimally exit simultaneously (clustering). These features are absent when monopoly is always preferred to exit.
item.dc:creator: Yukun Cao, Jan Palczewski

item.title: Thermodynamic Formalism for Non-Invariant Probabilities: Entropy, Divergence, Channels
item.description: arXiv:2611.13904v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ denote, respectively, the sets of Borel and $\sigma$-invariant probabilities on the uncountable set $\Omega=\{1,2,...,d\}^\mathbb{N}$. Given a H\"older Jacobian $J$, the dual Ruelle operator $\mu \in \mathcal{M} \mapsto \mathcal{L}_{J}^* (\mu)$ will play the role of a dynamical channel; generalizes the action of a stochastic matrix on probability vectors. Since $\mathcal{L}_{J}^*$ generally breaks $\sigma$-invariance, we introduce the \emph{ni-entropy} $h_{ni}(\mu)$ for non-invariant measures, employing the concept of the expected value function on cylinders of size one. $h_{ni}(\mu)$ differs from Shannon entropy but extends the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy from $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ to $\mathcal{M}$; $h_{ni}$ is concave and u.s.c. This leads us to the concept of ni-pressure $\mathcal{P}(A)$ of a potential $A:\Omega \to \mathbb{R}$. $\mu\in \mathcal{M}$ is not a density with respect to a dominating measure. We define an {\it ni-Kullback-Leibler divergence} $D_{ni}(\rho || \nu)$ not assuming absolute continuity. We investigate concepts of Information Theory such as Minimal Output Entropy, Donsker-Varadhan variational principle, a variational formula for $h_{ni}$, bounds for divergence, information projections, and their connections to the ni-pressure $\mathcal{P}$.
item.dc:creator: Artur O. Lopes, Elismar R. Oliveira

item.title: On Monotonicity in Mean Field Games Induced by Discount Factor Transformations
item.description: arXiv:2611.13939v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper is devoted to the well-posedness of a class of infinite horizon discounted Mean Field Games (MFGs) problems, where both an exponential discount and a so-called cheap control factors are present simultaneously, and scale in a possibly different way. We introduce a new class of transformations of variables, at the level of both the MFG PDE and the corresponding FBSDE systems. We then show how these transformations reveal a new mechanism that generates semiconvexity estimates for the value function and ensures the existence of mean field equilibria, as long as the parameters land in a suitable regime, that we quantitatively describe. This new mechanism demonstrates furthermore how discount factors lead to a source of strong displacement monotonicity for the Lagrangian, without any initial monotonicity assumptions on the running costs. Consequently, in such regimes of parameters uniqueness of solutions manifests. Our approach uses a Lagrangian point of view, which lets us treat general non-separable Lagrangians and both deterministic and idiosyncratic noise driven models in a transparent, unified way. For a specific class of quadratic Lagrangians, using turnpike-type methods, we further obtain an exponential contractivity estimate for the mean field equilibria.
item.dc:creator: Elisa Continelli, Nicol\`o De Bernardi, Hei Jie Lam, Alp\'ar R. M\'esz\'aros

item.title: A stochastic chemical system in contact with reservoirs
item.description: arXiv:2611.14192v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we analyse the behaviour of a non-reversible stochastic chemical system obtained as an approximation of a stochastic chemical system in which the concentration of some chemicals is higher than the concentration of the other chemicals. The master equation associated with this approximated system is characterised by a discrete part, modelling the reactions among chemicals that have low concentration, by a transport term and a diffusion term. The transport-diffusion terms describe the fluctuations in the concentration of abundant chemicals. The model contains a second order term is of order {\epsilon}, that describes the fluctuation in the concentrations of the abundand substances. We prove that the master equation has a spectral gap that is independent on $\epsilon$ and we analyse in detail the asymptotics of the solution to the master equation as $\epsilon \to 0$.
item.dc:creator: Eugenia Franco, Jann Hendrik Schr\"oders, Juan J. L. Vel\'azquez

item.title: Deep Learning for Operator Maps in Optimal Liquidation
item.description: arXiv:2611.14245v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyze the solution map of a optimal execution problem in which price dynamics are subject to a general transient impact kernel. Given the structure of the optimal trading strategy derived by Abi Jaber and Neuman in \cite{https://doi.org/10.1111/mafi.12465}, we show that the strategy is locally Lipschitz continuous with respect to the underlying model parameters governing temporary and transient price impact as well as the fundamental price process. Continuity of this map justifies the application of neural-net based approximations which take model parameters as inputs. We propose a method generating samples of the transient price impact kernel for the purposes of creating training data, and a method of projecting the kernel to a finite dimensional representation appropriate for input to a neural net, and a dimensional reduction based on the relationship between inventory and trade signal. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the trained neural net and use it to quantify the potential financial costs associated with misspecifying the transient impact kernel.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Donnelly, Luca Galimberti, Brian Healy, Siqi Zhang

item.title: On the geometry of Gaussian Mean Shift Detection
item.description: arXiv:2611.14264v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the problem of detecting a shift in the mean of a standard Gaussian random vector, where the direction of the shift belongs to an arbitrary subset $T$ of the Euclidean unit sphere. We introduce a correlation functional $\kappa(T)$ and establish a general lower bound on the detection radius in terms of this functional. We identify regularity conditions under which this lower bound is optimal up to an absolute constant. As an application, we recover some well-known results in the literature such as the detection radius for $s$-sparse unit vectors.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Abdalla, Grigoris Paouris, Roman Vershynin

item.title: Poisson boundaries of lattices in locally compact groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.14321v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a random walk on a general locally compact group we provide a discretization procedure transforming the walk to one on a lattice of the group, preserving the Poisson boundary and some finiteness of moments.
item.dc:creator: Antoine Derimay

item.title: The strongly local part of nonlinear Dirichlet structures and its energy measures
item.description: arXiv:2611.14400v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper substantially extends the results of Sasaya (2026, JFA): we propose a framework for nonlinear generalizations of regular Dirichlet forms and prove that each energy in this framework has a largest strongly local part. We also prove the existence and uniqueness of canonical energy measures of this part, which satisfy convexity and locality properties and, under additional assumptions, certain chain rules in one variable. In particular, our framework requires neither $p$-homogeneity nor strong locality. Moreover, under a Ball--Carlen--Lieb-type upper bound, we prove more detailed chain rules for the directional derivatives of these energy measures. Our framework is applicable both to $p$-energy forms on fractals and to a class of symmetric nonlinear Dirichlet forms in the sense of Cipriani and Grillo~\cite{CG2003}, including those of Orlicz--Sobolev and variable-exponent Sobolev type.
item.dc:creator: K\^ohei Sasaya

item.title: Supercritical Liouville quantum gravity and CLE$_4$
item.description: arXiv:2308.11832v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the first relationship between Schramm-Loewner evolution (SLE) and Liouville quantum gravity (LQG) in the supercritical (a.k.a. strongly coupled) phase, which corresponds to central charge values $\mathbf c_{\mathrm L} \in (1,25)$ or equivalently to complex values of $\gamma$ with $|\gamma|=2$. More precisely, we introduce a canonical supercritical LQG surface with the topology of the disk. We then show that for each $\mathbf c_{\mathrm L} \in (1,25)$ there is a coupling of this LQG surface with a conformal loop ensemble with parameter $\kappa=4$ (CLE$_4$) wherein the LQG surfaces parametrized by the regions enclosed by the CLE$_4$ loops are conditionally independent supercritical LQG disks given their boundary lengths. In this coupling, the CLE$_4$ is neither determined by nor independent from the LQG. Guided by our coupling result, we exhibit a combinatorially natural family of loop-decorated random planar maps whose scaling limit we conjecture to be the supercritical LQG disk coupled to CLE$_4$. We include a substantial list of open problems.
item.dc:creator: Morris Ang, Ewain Gwynne

item.title: Large Deviations Principle for Bures-Wasserstein Barycenters
item.description: arXiv:2409.11384v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the large deviations principle for empirical Bures-Wasserstein barycenters of independent, identically-distributed samples of covariance matrices and covariance operators. As an application, we explore some consequences of our results for the phenomenon of dimension-free concentration of measure for Bures-Wasserstein barycenters. Our theory reveals a novel notion of exponential tilting in the Bures-Wasserstein space, which, in analogy with Cram\'er's theorem in the Euclidean case, solves the relative entropy projection problem under a constraint on the barycenter. Notably, this method of proof is easy to adapt to other geometric settings of interest; with the same method, we obtain large deviations principles for empirical barycenters in Riemannian manifolds and the univariate Wasserstein space, and we obtain large deviations upper bounds for empirical barycenters in the general multivariate Wasserstein space. In fact, our results are the first known large deviations principles for Fr\'echet means in any non-linear metric space.
item.dc:creator: Adam Quinn Jaffe, Leonardo V. Santoro

item.title: A functional central limit theorem for weighted occupancy processes of the Karlin model
item.description: arXiv:2412.02160v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A functional central limit theorem is established for weighted occupancy processes of the Karlin model. The weighted occupancy processes take the form of, with $D_{n,j}$ denoting the number of urns with $j$-balls after the first $n$ samplings, $\sum_{j=1}^na_jD_{n,j}$ for a prescribed sequence of real numbers $(a_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}$. The main applications are limit theorems for random permutations induced by Chinese restaurant processes with $(\alpha,\theta)$-seating with $\alpha\in(0,1), \theta>-\alpha$. An example is briefly mentioned here, and full details are provided in an accompanying paper.
item.dc:creator: Jaime Garza, Yizao Wang

item.title: A Tail-Respecting Splitting Numerical Scheme for L\'evy-Driven SDEs With Superlinear Drifts
item.description: arXiv:2504.07255v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present an explicit numerical approximation scheme, denoted by $\{X^n\}$, for the effective simulation of solutions $X$ to a multivariate stochastic differential equation (SDE) with a superlinearly growing $\kappa$-dissipative drift, where $\kappa>1$, driven by a multiplicative heavy-tailed L\'evy process that has a finite $p$-th moment, with $p>0$. We show that the strong $L^{p_X}$-convergence $\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\mathbf E \|X^n_t-X_t\|^{p_X}=\mathcal O (h_n^{\gamma})$ holds for any $p_X\in (0,p+\kappa-1)$, which is exactly the range where the $p_X$-moment of the solution is known to be finite. Additionally, for any $p_X\in (0,p)$ we establish strong uniform convergence: $\mathbf E\sup_{t\in[0,T]} \|X^n_t-X_t\|^{p_X}=\mathcal{O} ( h_n^{\delta} )$. In both cases we determine the convergence rates $\gamma$ and $\delta$. In the special case of SDEs driven solely by a Brownian motion, our numerical scheme preserves super-exponential moments of the solution. The scheme $\{X^n\}$ is realized as a combination of a well-known Euler method with a Lie-Trotter type splitting technique.
item.dc:creator: Olga Aryasova, Oleksii Kulyk, Ilya Pavlyukevich

item.title: Harmonic problems arising from continuous time random walks limit processes
item.description: arXiv:2505.14550v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we develop a universal method that identifies the (non-local) governing evolution equations for Continuous Time Random Walks' (CTRWs) limit processes. Given one of these processes, our method provides the form of a non-local operator, acting on space and time variables jointly, such that the (generalized) harmonic problem associated with it represents an evolution governing equation for this process. Then, the well-posedness of this problem must be established case by case. In this paper, we establish well-posedness when the process is a Feller process (on a locally compact separable metric space $E$) time-changed with the overshooting of a subordinator. Also, we will show how our method applies to several cases when the equation and its well-posedness are already known, hence unifying several different approaches in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Bio\v{c}i\'c, Bruno Toaldo

item.title: A functional Breuer--Major theorem with Poisson noise and a sharp regularity condition
item.description: arXiv:2510.26216v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We extend the functional Breuer--Major theorem to stationary sequences generated from a Poisson point process under a regularity condition on the nonlinearity. We use the $L^p$ spectral gap inequality of the Poisson point process to prove the tightness. Our use of the spectral gap inequality naturally requires a regularity condition. In contrast to the Gaussian case, this condition cannot in general be replaced by integrability alone. We construct an example at the critical regularity showing that the regularity condition is necessary and the regularity threshold is sharp.
item.dc:creator: Fanhao Kong, Haiyi Wang

item.title: Marked stable L\'evy processes in Brownian local time
item.description: arXiv:2512.05466v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a random partition of the (local) time-space half-plane $\mathbb R_+\times \mathbb R$, measurable with respect to a single Brownian motion. The construction is driven by two objects canonically associated with this Brownian path: a white noise driving a pair of coupled squared Bessel flows whose parameters differ by $\delta\in (0,2)$, and a continuous space-filling exploration of the half-plane. Exceptional bifurcation points of the coupled flows generate a random partition of the half-plane, up to a zero-measure gasket, whose widths are squared Bessel excursions with negative parameter $(-\delta)$. A suitable time-change of the Brownian exploration arranges these excursions, in exploration order, as marks attached to the jumps of a spectrally positive stable L\'evy process of index $(1+\delta/2)$. As applications, we recover the interval partition evolutions of [Forman et. al. 2020] as horizontal slices of our construction, and use this representation to prove the independence between their total mass evolution and normalized partition evolution, as conjectured in [Forman et. al. 2021]. We also prove that the gasket of our partition is homeomorphic to the half-plane analogue of the stable shredded sphere introduced in [Bj\"ornberg, Curien and Stef\'ansson 2022].
item.dc:creator: Elie A\"id\'ekon, Quan Shi, Chengshi Wang

item.title: Persistence of the Wiener sausage: sampling stability and limit theorems for Betti-curve functionals of drifted planar Brownian motion
item.description: arXiv:2604.03130v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the persistent homology of the offset filtration generated by the range of a planar Brownian motion with constant nonzero drift (Wiener sausages of increasing radius). We prove what are, to our knowledge, the first law of large numbers and central limit theorem for its smoothed Betti-curve functionals. For every bounded Borel weight $\psi$ supported in a compact radius window $[r_0,r_1]\subset(0,\infty)$, the functional $\Phi_\psi(T)=\int_{r_0}^{r_1}\beta_1(T,r)\psi(r)\,dr$, where $\beta_1(T,r)$ counts the holes of the radius-$r$ sausage at time $T$, satisfies $\Phi_\psi(T)/T\to\rho_\psi$ almost surely and in every $L^p$, for a deterministic constant $\rho_\psi$. This yields a finite positive Betti-curve intensity measure on the radius axis, which we identify as absolutely continuous through a fixed-radius law of large numbers along regeneration times, valid at almost every radius. We also prove Gaussian fluctuations at scale $\sqrt{T}$, for one weight and jointly for finitely many, with a Green-Kubo variance over the regeneration cycles. The proof combines a renewal structure along the drift direction, obtained by the method of Sznitman and Zerner without invoking the strong Markov property at the cut times, with a Mayer-Vietoris control of the non-additivity of topology under concatenation and a deterministic bound on the integrated hole count of a planar offset proved in a companion paper. A sampling theorem bounds the bottleneck distance between the diagram of the continuous filtration and that of a time-sampled point cloud by the pathwise modulus of continuity, placing these objects in a data-analytic framework.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Guillaume

item.title: The inradius law for the cavities of planar Brownian motion, with applications to the Wiener sausage
item.description: arXiv:2606.11248v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: ```text Let $K_1=B[0,1]$ be the trace of a planar Brownian motion, and let $N_{\mathrm{in}}(\eta)$ be the number of its cavities, the bounded components of $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus K_1$, whose inradius exceeds $\eta$. We prove that, almost surely and in $L^p$ for every $p\in[1,2]$, $\eta^2(\log(1/\eta))^2 N_{\mathrm{in}}(\eta)\to c_{\mathrm{in}}=\frac{\pi}{2}\int G^2 d\mathcal{L}\in(0,\frac12]$, where $G$ is the ratio of the inradius of a shape to the square root of its area and $\mathcal{L}$ is Werner's limiting shape law. The inradius, and not the area by which the cavities have been counted classically, decides survival under thickening: a cavity contains a hole of the Wiener sausage of radius $r$ if and only if its inradius exceeds $r$. Through Brownian scaling, the number $\beta_1^T(r)$ of holes of the sausage of radius $r$ of $B[0,T]$, the Betti curve of its degree-one persistent homology, is bounded below at the scale $T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$, with the identified constant $4c_{\mathrm{in}}$ in expectation and with any smaller constant with probability tending to one. A matching upper bound cannot follow from any general bound in terms of perimeter, area, diameter or length; we prove that it is equivalent to a first-moment estimate for near-critical pockets, the holes at level $\eta$ on which the distance to the trace is at most $2\eta$. That estimate is proved in a companion paper, so that the expected number of holes is of exact order $T/(r^2(\log T)^2)$. ```
item.dc:creator: Tristan Guillaume (CY Cergy Paris University)

item.title: The $M/M_D/c$ queue with dependent servers: A canonical Markovian extension of $M/M/c$
item.description: arXiv:2606.24881v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The classical $M/M/c$ queue is the canonical Markovian model for a single-node queue with Poisson arrivals and homogeneous independent servers. We identify its natural counterpart when the servers are dependent. For homogeneous Markovian labelled service-completion mechanisms (retaining the identities of the completing servers), consistency under restriction to subsets of busy servers is equivalent to an independent Poisson shock representation, yielding homogeneous Marshall--Olkin multivariate exponential residual-service laws. This characterization identifies the $M/M_D/c$ queue as the canonical Markovian extension of $M/M/c$ to dependent homogeneous servers, with a Markovian queue-length process. For heterogeneous servers, augmenting boundary states with busy-server identities yields a Markovian queue-state process, as in the classical independent-server setting. For arbitrary $c$ and fixed idle-set assignment, we derive an explicit matrix-analytic stationary solution and departure and customer-delay laws. Waiting time conditional on delay is exponential, and the stationary sojourn distribution has a phase-type representation with at most $c+1$ phases. A three-server comparison with identical bivariate residual-service laws demonstrates how higher-order dependence can change waiting-time behavior.
item.dc:creator: Qihui Bu, Suman Thapa, Yiqiang Q. Zhao

item.title: Spectral Characterisation of Covariance Existence in Markov-Switching Affine Recurrences
item.description: arXiv:2607.09994v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper provides a finite-dimensional spectral characterisation of covariance existence for finite-state Markov-switching affine recurrences of the form \[ Z_{n+1}=A_{\Theta_{n+1}}Z_n+\zeta_{n+1}. \] While strict stationarity is typically governed by negativity of the top Lyapunov exponent of the random matrix products, this does not ensure finite variances, covariances, or Pearson correlations. We show that these second-order properties are governed instead by a Markov-switching Kronecker operator. Writing \(T_{ji}:=p_{ij}(A_j\otimes A_j)\) and denoting its spectral radius by \(\rho(T)\), we prove that, under a natural Perron-excitation condition on the innovation covariance, \(\rho(T)<1\) is necessary and sufficient for the stationary solution to be square-integrable. When this condition holds, the regime-weighted second moments solve a finite-dimensional linear system, yielding the covariance matrix explicitly. Thus, the mean-square spectral condition becomes an exact covariance-existence criterion for the stationary law. Examples illustrate the separation: the top Lyapunov exponent may be negative while the second-order spectral radius exceeds one, so strict stationarity can persist even when finite second moments, and hence population covariances and Pearson correlations, do not exist.
item.dc:creator: Wilson Tai

item.title: Cutoff for q-deformed classical card shuffles in the type A Iwahori--Hecke algebra
item.description: arXiv:2609.13570v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the mixing behavior of three q-deformed card shuffles on $\mathcal{H}_q(S_n)$: the short systematic scan introduced in \cite{DiaconisRam2000}, the $q$--deformed random--to--random shuffle introduced in \cite{AxelrodFreedBraunerChiangComminsLang2024}, and the $q$--deformed $k$--star transposition shuffle, whose $q=1$ counterpart was studied in \cite{ArfaeeNestoridi}. The first two chains were diagonalized in \cite{DiaconisRam2000} and \cite{AxelrodFreedBraunerChiangComminsLang2024}, respectively. Here, we diagonalize the $q$--deformed $k$--star transposition shuffle and use the spectra of the three chains to study their mixing behavior. For fixed $q>1$, we prove that all three exhibit total variation and $\ell^2$ cutoff. For the short systematic scan, these improve both the upper and lower bounds of Diaconis and Ram \cite{DiaconisRam2000}.
item.dc:creator: Samira Arfaee, Bryan Wong

item.title: Bernoulli flow for Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graphs
item.description: arXiv:2609.15566v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the adjacency matrix $A$ of the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graph $\mathbb G(N,p)$ in the regime $Np \gg (\log N)^2$. We establish optimal isotropic delocalization for the bulk eigenvectors $\boldsymbol u$, meaning that $\langle \boldsymbol v, \boldsymbol u\rangle^2 \leq \frac{C \log N}{N}$ with very high probability for any deterministic normalized $\boldsymbol v$. In addition, we prove local spectral universality in the bulk by showing that the local spectral statistics coincide with those of the GOE. The main tool of our proof is a local law for the resolvent of $A$, down to optimal spectral scales and with optimal error bounds. Its proof relies on a new approach to local laws that we call the Bernoulli flow. It is a characteristic flow method in which the usual Brownian process is replaced by a Bernoulli process, where each edge of the graph forms an independent Markov process that jumps at unit rate from closed to open. The spectral parameter flows according to a suitably constructed matrix-valued Bernoulli characteristic flow.
item.dc:creator: Joscha Henheik, Antti Knowles

item.title: Fitting Gaussian vectors in normed spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.20299v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a family of $N$ i.i.d. Gaussian points in a $d$-dimensional normed space, what is the probability that some linear transformation maps it to the unit sphere? The case of a Euclidean space is known as the ellipsoid fitting problem and has recently attracted major attention. We initiate a study of this fitting problem in a general normed space, both asymptotically and in a fixed dimension. We specifically focus on the space $\ell_\infty^d$, where a combinatorial reformulation allows us to show that $cd^2/\log d$ points can be fitted with high probability. We illustrate that the geometry of the normed space is reflected in the fitting problem by showing that in dimension $2$, the spaces $\ell_2^2$ and $\ell_\infty^2$ are characterized by having extremal fittability properties. We also study the probability that a family of $N$ i.i.d.\ Gaussian points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is in convex position and show that a sharp threshold occurs around the value $N=\exp(d/2e)$.
item.dc:creator: Guillaume Aubrun, Emmanouil Stavrakakis

item.title: Free energy and fluctuations of generalized bipartite Sherrington-Kirkpatrick models and generalized Hopfield models
item.description: arXiv:2610.29055v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the free energy of generalized bipartite Sherrington-Kirkpatrick models in the high temperature regime, with one spin normalized and the other either normalized or i.i.d. We derive a unified formula for the limiting free energy in both settings. We also prove that the fluctuations of the free energy converge to a Gaussian distribution under mild assumptions. The proof is based on a bipartite multigraph expansion, which also gives free energy results for generalized Hopfield models and log likelihood ratio of spiked rectangular models.
item.dc:creator: Hyunsuk Choo, Ji Oon Lee

item.title: Invariant universal averages and Bertrand's paradox: a response to Shackel
item.description: arXiv:2611.00981v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 2014, with D. Aerts we proposed a solution to the hard problem of Bertrand's paradox by means of a universal average over different ways of randomizing an entity. In his recent monograph, N. Shackel raises objections concerning the approximation by cellular densities, the restrictions used in their construction, the apparently trivial limit of their averages, the choice of a second-order probability law, and the dependence of the result on the naming of chords. We revisit these objections using the invariance-based formulation of the universal average. The first objection is well taken, and the approximation argument is repaired: an explicit sequence of bivalent cellular densities provides weak approximation of any prescribed probability measure, with an error bound for intervals. We show that any second-order selection law invariant under rearrangements of equal-length cells has the same uniform barycenter, independently of the particular densities and weights employed. For cellular densities, this conclusion holds exactly at every finite resolution. Thus, non-uniqueness of the second-order law does not prevent uniqueness of the average it produces, which is what entitles one to speak of 'the' universal average at all. Finally, we prove that no probability measure can be invariant under both these rearrangements and arbitrary changes of interval lengths. The reference geometry therefore cannot be obtained by averaging alone: it must be supplied by the physical modelization of the randomized entity. These results clarify the scope, and the limitations, of our original distinction between the easy and hard problems of Bertrand's paradox.
item.dc:creator: Massimiliano Sassoli de Bianchi

item.title: Uniform Central Limit Theorems for Degree Distributions of Sparse Graphon Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.06892v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The degree distribution is among the most basic summaries of a network, yet no functional limit theorem for the empirical degree distribution of graphon models has been available, even for dense, bounded graphons, for which only finite-dimensional results were known. We study the empirical degree distribution of sparse $L^p$ graphon models, allowing unbounded kernels and hence heavy-tailed degrees. For graphons whose latent expected degrees have a density, we prove a finite-dimensional central limit theorem whenever $n\rho_n/\log n\to\infty$ and $n\rho_n^{2+\beta}\to0$, where $\rho_n$ is the sparsity level and the kernel has $2+\beta$ moments for some $\beta>0$; the limiting covariance coincides with that of the dense case. Under additional local regularity, we establish a functional central limit theorem on compact intervals in the interior of the support. Under tail regularity and a stronger sparsity condition, we prove that uniformity extends to unbounded intervals. We also show that uniform limits fail at atoms of the degree distribution, for instance in stochastic block models. The analysis rests on an exact multilinear representation of the conditional degree distribution, which identifies its Hoeffding decomposition without Edgeworth expansions, combined with a lattice version of Billingsley's tightness criterion and moment inequalities of Efron-Stein type.
item.dc:creator: Robert Lunde, Soumendra Lahiri

item.title: Nonparametric estimation of linear multiplier for SDEs driven by generalized stochastic volatility
item.description: arXiv:2412.00005v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the problem of nonparametric estimation of the linear multiplier function $\theta(t)$ for processes satisfying stochastic differential equations of the type $$dX_t= \theta(t)X_t dt+ \epsilon\; \sigma(t,X_t,Y_t)dW_t, X_0=x_0, 0 \leq t \leq T$$ based on the observation of the process $\{X_t, 0\leq t \leq T\}$ and investigate the asymptotic properties of the estimator as the small noise $\epsilon$ tends to zero. Here $\{W_t, t\geq 0\}$ is the standard Brownian motion and $\{Y_t, t\geq 0\}$ is a process adapted to the filtration generated by the Brownian motion.
item.dc:creator: B. L. S Prakasa Rao

item.title: Random tree Besov priors: Data-driven regularisation parameter selection
item.description: arXiv:2601.12957v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a data-driven algorithm for automatically selecting the wavelet density parameters in Bayesian inversion under random tree Besov priors. One of the key challenges in Bayesian inversion is the construction of priors that are both expressive and computationally feasible. Random tree Besov priors, introduced in \cite{Kekkonen2023}, provide a flexible framework for capturing local regularity properties and sparsity patterns in a wavelet basis. In this paper, we extend this approach by introducing a hierarchical model that enables data-driven selection of the wavelet density parameter, allowing the regularisation strength to adapt across scales while retaining computational efficiency. We focus on nonparametric regression and also present preliminary plug-and-play results for a deconvolution problem.
item.dc:creator: Hanne Kekkonen, Andreas Tataris

item.title: Minimax Optimal Estimation of Transport-Growth Pairs in Unbalanced Optimal Transport
item.description: arXiv:2605.08705v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Unbalanced optimal transport extends classical optimal transport to measures with different total masses, but statistical guarantees for estimation of the transport map and the growth map remain limited. We study unbalanced optimal transport with quadratic cost and Kullback-Leibler marginal penalties and argue that the natural target of estimation is a transport-growth pair. Consequently, we develop two estimators for the transport-growth pair under two setups: a nearest-neighbor estimator for transporting between general densities, and a kernel-based estimator for transporting between smooth densities. We prove that the kernel-based estimator achieves the minimax optimal rate up to a logarithmic factor by deriving a matching lower bound on the minimax risk. Our main technical contribution is a reduction of estimation to a stability bound on the unbalanced optimal transport value. This bound controls the transport map and growth map risks through the duality gap of the true dual potentials for the estimated measures. These results provide a statistical foundation for estimation of the transport-growth pair in unbalanced optimal transport.
item.dc:creator: Donlapark Ponnoprat, Noboru Isobe, Masaaki Imaizumi

item.title: Maximum Probability of Independence in Transitive Matroids
item.description: arXiv:2605.23291v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $M$ be a matroid on a finite ground set $E$, and suppose that the automorphism group of $M$ acts transitively on $E$. We show the following: if $X_1,\ldots,X_K$ are sampled independently from a distribution $p$ on $E$, then the probability that the samples are distinct and that $\{X_1,\ldots,X_K\}$ is an independent set in $M$ is quasi-concave in $p$ and maximized when $p$ is uniform. For $2\le K\le\rank(M)$, we characterize all maximizers by uniform total mass on the parallel classes and, in particular, show that the maximizer is unique and has global quadratic stability when $M$ is simple. As a corollary, for a random $K\times N$ matrix over a finite field with i.i.d.\ rows, uniform sampling from the nonzero vectors maximizes the probability of full row rank. Finally, we show that uniform sampling maximizes $\Prob\big(\rank_M(X_1,\ldots,X_L)\ge r\big)$, and hence also $\E\rank_M(X_1,\ldots,X_L)$, for every $L, r$.
item.dc:creator: Mladen Kova\v{c}evi\'c

item.title: Resolution of Vinzant's Conjecture on Phase Retrieval Injectivity
item.description: arXiv:2606.17922v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $A\in\mathbb C^{N\times M}$ with $N=4M-5$ has independent standard complex Gaussian entries. We prove that the probability that the phase retrieval map generated by $A$ is injective is strictly smaller than $1$, and is $O(M^{-1})$ as $M\to \infty$. This proves a conjecture of Cynthia Vinzant, which was later restated by Afonso S. Bandeira in \cite{bandeira2026randomstrasse101}. The main result of this paper was obtained using generative AI, in particular GPT6-Astra, GPT 5.6-sol, and the Rethlas system.
item.dc:creator: Zhangsong Li

item.title: 3-Neighbor bootstrap percolation on two-dimensional grids
item.description: arXiv:2608.06133v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the $3$-neighbor bootstrap percolation process, a vertex becomes (and remains) infected if at least three of its neighbors are infected. We say that an initial configuration of infected vertices percolates if eventually all vertices are infected. We exactly determine the size of the minimum percolating set for the $3$-neighbor bootstrap percolation process on all remaining open cases for rectangular grid graphs $P_m\square P_n$. This extends earlier work of Dukes, Noel, and Romer.
item.dc:creator: Neal Bushaw, Alexander Clifton

item.title: Thin-Shell implies small-ball deviation via Gaussian tilts
item.description: arXiv:2608.20816v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that uniform thin-shell estimates for isotropic log-concave measures $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ yield precise and explicit deviation estimates for the Euclidean norm $|X|$ below the expectation, improving the square-root dependence of Klartag-Lehec to a quadratic one (which is best possible, up to numeric constants). Using the recent Chen-Klartag sharp variance bound, we deduce: $$ \mu\left(|X|\le \sqrt{n}-s\right) \le \exp\left\{ -\frac{s^2}{4} \left(1+O\left(\frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}\right)\right) \right\} \qquad \forall\, s\in(0,\sqrt{n}). $$ In particular, this yields a new and transparent proof that Thin-Shell implies Slicing (by passing through small-ball estimates). Our method is based on using central Gaussian tilts, recently introduced by Brazitikos, which may be thought of as a deterministic version of Eldan's stochastic localization. An anisotropic variant (when $\mu$ has general covariance structure) of these deviation estimates is also obtained.
item.dc:creator: Silouanos Brazitikos, Emanuel Milman

item.title: Banded Totally Positive Matrices and Positive Bidiagonal Factorizations: Existence, Stability, and Toeplitz Orthogonality
item.description: arXiv:2610.08568v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A positive bidiagonal factorization of a banded totally positive matrix expresses it as a product of unit lower and upper bidiagonal factors with positive off-diagonal entries and a positive diagonal matrix. In finite dimension such factorizations always exist, with parameter domains defined by polynomial inequalities. In the semi-infinite case, existence is equivalent to convergence of explicit positive series. Every bounded banded totally positive matrix is an operator-norm limit of matrices admitting these factorizations, through perturbations confined to a fixed initial block. Necessary and sufficient criteria characterize analytic dependence of prescribed factors on perturbations. With fixed initial entries, a relative entrywise criterion allows unbounded factors with different growth rates. For uniformly positive bounded factors with variable initial entries, the criterion involves every pair of factors on each triangular side and the signed triangular inverses. The dimensions of the local factorization families are determined. Normalized LDU factors depend analytically at every interior point of the factorization class. For banded totally positive Toeplitz matrices, a stable positive bidiagonal factorization exists if and only if the symbol polynomial has distinct roots. Root formulas give two polynomial vector families with mixed-type multiple orthogonality for a rectangular matrix of positive measures. One factorization simultaneously attains the smallest possible first off-diagonal entries of both normalization matrices. The weighted linear forms are independent of the factorization. Their Chebyshev expansions yield asymptotic zero spacing inside the support and convergence of normalized kernels to the sine kernel after rescaling by the local zero density.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Ma\~nas

item.title: Moments of Magic Squares: Line-Sum Conditions, a Permutation Threshold, and Random Energies
item.description: arXiv:2610.38386v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Every semi-magic square of order $n$ satisfies the axial moment identities $\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}j^m=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}i^m=M(n)\sum_jj^m$ for all $m\ge1$, where $M(n)=n(n^2+1)/2$. For real matrices the converse requires $1\le m\le n-1$, whereas for arrangements of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ fewer moments suffice once $n\ge14$. We define the permutation threshold $k^*(n)$ as the least $k$ such that every arrangement satisfying these identities for $1\le m\le k$ is semi-magic. In terms of the column-sum deviations $\gamma_j$, the degree-$k$ conditions state that $\sum_j\gamma_jt^j$ is divisible by $(t-1)^{k+1}$, linking $k^*(n)$ to the Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem. While Schur's bound on real zeros gives $k^*(n)\le\sqrt{2(n-1)\log(n^4/4)}$, we prove the converse realisability bound $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt n$ (and $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt6-o(1))\sqrt n$ when $4\mid n$) by perturbing semi-magic squares with complementary row pairs via horizontal swaps. We also show that $k^*(n)=n-1$ for $3\le n\le13$, $k^*(n)=n-2$ for $14\le n\le17$, and $k^*(n)\le n-3$ for $n\ge18$, and determine $k^*(n)$ for $18\le n\le40$ with computer assistance. Finally, at the $k=1$ level of the hierarchy, we specialise the Mantel--Hubert quadratic assignment variance formula to obtain exact means, variances, and limit laws under a uniform random arrangement for the full line-sum energy $E_{\mathrm{full}}$, for the four-term energy $E_4$ combining the first moments and the two diagonals, and for Loly's moment of inertia, and find that $|L_4|=14,639,440$ arrangements of order $4$ satisfy $E_4=0$.
